Consult Summary:
- Empiric treatment for suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection presenting with dysuria, midline lower abdominal pain, and hematuria; plan includes a 3-day antibiotic course and supportive measures.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dysuria with painful urination for six days; foul-smelling urine; visible blood in urine; midline lower abdominal pain rated 7/10, intermittent.
- Associated symptoms: No fever; able to pass urine; no loin pain; no vaginal discharge.
- Onset/progression: Symptoms began six days ago and have persisted with variable intensity.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS); no other medical problems reported.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.
- Medications: Mebeverine (200 mg), taken three times daily.
- Social history: Lives with friends; works as a support worker; drinks alcohol occasionally (about one glass of wine per week); non-smoker.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- (No physical examination findings or vital signs provided.)

Impression:
- Suspected urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) without fever.

Plan:
- Treatment: Empiric 3-day course of antibiotics for presumed UTI; prescription to be sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy (antibiotic name not specified in transcript; start as soon as possible).
- Counseling and home care: Encourage increased fluid intake (2.5–3 liters/day); cranberry juice optional; urine-acidity sachets available from chemist.
- Monitoring: Check temperature with a home thermometer; if symptoms worsen, fever develops, or unable to pass urine, contact again; if symptoms persist or recur after completing course, follow up for re-evaluation.
- Testing: Urine testing not required at this time given clinical presentation.
- Follow-up: No need to call after finishing if symptoms resolve; if recurrent episodes occur, re-evaluate.
- Pharmacy logistics: Pharmacy selected (Knightsbridge Practice) and prescription will be available for pickup; pickup anticipated in about an hour; patient plans to collect at lunchtime.
